bug_semantics: is_url_safe delegates host classification to is_hostname_resolve_to_internal_ip, whose resolve_all_records helper originally queried dns.resolve4, dns.resolve6, and dns.resolveCname only. When an explicitly configured resolver such as 1.1.1.1 returns NXDOMAIN for localhost, those calls produce empty arrays; is_hostname_resolve_to_internal_ip then returns false for 'internal', so is_url_safe accepts the loopback URL and enables SSRF. The fix falls back to OS dns.lookup when both A and AAAA resolver results are empty, recovering localhost's loopback address for rejection.
flaw_origin: Commit 6885ccae01fbc1f2ca596faf50d541cddcfb671a created src/helpers.ts and first introduced both the resolver-only resolve_all_records implementation and the fail-open 'if (ips.length === 0) return false' hostname-classification path. Its sole parent 9901fff9a4bca05fa99fc311f9e57971c33c17ff has no src/helpers.ts path, so the vulnerable mechanism is absent from the immediate parent. Exact-string history, git log -L, and blame converge on this atomic public first-write; GitHub reports no associated pull request for the commit, so there is no public squash/member history to decompose.

git show 668c21792cd1252baf779a176aa652e2b4c0067d changes src/helpers.ts so empty A and AAAA results trigger dns.lookup(host, { all: true }) and append returned IPv4/IPv6 addresses before internal-IP classification; its parent 2eef49dc0fc3a864e566f44bf6cf9c95e4410798 still has the vulnerable resolver-only code.

The published npm 1.0.4 tarball https://registry.npmjs.org/dssrf/-/dssrf-1.0.4.tgz has dist/helpers.js calling resolve4 with no lookup fallback, whereas https://registry.npmjs.org/dssrf/-/dssrf-1.0.5.tgz contains the dns.lookup fallback, directly confirming the affected/patched package boundary.

Commit 9481e4e4bac7660fcad4e0075844c4374644d0ca mirrors the TypeScript fix into dist/helpers.js immediately after 668c21792cd1252baf779a176aa652e2b4c0067d; version bump commit 68c3569354fc838b0888a84feec636e621f195dc sets package.json to 1.0.5 and contains both commits in its ancestry.
reasoning: The advisory and published package artifacts establish a real SSRF lifecycle: npm 1.0.4 ships resolver-only lookup and can misclassify localhost as safe after NXDOMAIN, while 1.0.5 ships the fallback. Starting from the advisory's direct fix hunk, line history and blame trace the exact flawed helper and fail-open caller to 6885ccae01fbc1f2ca596faf50d541cddcfb671a. Direct parent-tree verification proves the entire source file, hence the vulnerable lines, absent at 9901fff9a4bca05fa99fc311f9e57971c33c17ff; no earlier move or public PR member exists to displace that BIC. Commit 668c21792cd1252baf779a176aa652e2b4c0067d is the smallest source fix, adding only the missing OS lookup fallback (with 9481e4e4bac7660fcad4e0075844c4374644d0ca updating the distributed JavaScript before the 1.0.5 bump). Finally, classification is based only on the BIC object: its human author/ordinary GitHub committer and trailer-free message provide no AI marker, so this real vulnerability is NOT_AI.
